1.1: Concerning the hidden teaching, which was spoken of old by Peter Fora, unto the hidden believers. The hidden teaching is as followeth: He who was before, and is; who came; who suffered; and died; and was buried; and rose again. He brake [the gates] of death; he opened [them]; and the dead arose. Was it not he alone who became man — whose flesh is of the Holy Spirit — for Adam, with his soul; who left not his soul in death; who in the Spirit called unto Adam, and made him live.

2.9: We believe the suffering of him who cannot suffer, who was born in the flesh, who cannot be born; dead, living; the Son of the Father; he was contained, who cannot be contained; who took away our sins, whereas in him there is no sin; dead, he lived;; through the sufferings of his flesh he redeemed us; and he gave us his honoured blood, the spirit of life, and the sanctification of the Spirit, and the water of our purification, even this.
2.10: Who giveth light within their hearts unto them that fear him; for their likeness endureth for ever; who and chose us out of all the ways of Satan, the pilot of souls;; we this;; he was, from before the world, with the Father; he saw the world in the enclosure of sin, when by the power of wisdom; he showed;;; unto death he was made to reign.
2.11: It pleased [him] to heal mankind; he was contained in the womb of the virgin, hidden from all the powers whose dwelling is in the heavens; and unto them that.
2.12: Flesh he put on, corruptible and incorruptible; for the flesh of the dead; incorruptible, which in appearance was the flesh of the dead;; the appearance, the incorruptible which is his, by a corruptible appearance was abolished.
2.13: And orders of righteousness by the Gospel he gave, who is the caller, that we might live; and by this Gospel the bonds of Satan were broken, that instead of death we might receive life as our portion, and instead of ignorance take understanding.
2.14: And he became man, the Son of the Lord; who was born of mortal man; he took what was first; to be born he was conceived as man.
2.15: This; and by the apostles he was preached; and by the angels he was praised; and by the prophet, all he was glorified.

3.16: He was crucified for our sake, and by his cross he became our life, our perfect [one]; by this, which is the hidden mystery, the perfect [one], which, which is in him.
3.17: No desire of man can remove the soul far from God; it cannot; whereas; glory; love does not turn away from God.
3.18: And by these lips the word cannot be precise [concerning] the things which diligently; hidden; now the mystery is revealed, unto the believers; not that it may be seen, but that it may be meditated; this is the cross; and in it let us glorify, that we may exalt [him].
3.19: And by it they that are baptized are perfect believers; they have saved their souls from all that was said, from all that appears but does not exist in reality.
3.20: By this, ye who shall become strong; examine yourselves, make deaf your ears; and for the things that appear make blind your eyes to what is manifest.
3.21: That ye may know the will of Jesus Christ, and all the mysteries of your salvation, O men and women, saints who are among you, in glorification in the Lord.
3.22: Let the inward man hear this. Christ put us under the yoke; he brought us near; having come, after he had suffered, he went down into Sheol, of the dead he took captive unto life. (the middle of the verse is textually corrupt; the edition declines to translate it) Who is this? Man he put on.

4.23: Who is this? Flesh was given; who is this who put on earth; who is this who in our likeness was born, and he is incorruptible?
4.24: Who is this who is a stranger to my law? Who is this who makes captive what is mine? Who is this who, by the power of the flame of fire, enters into struggle with death? Who is this who has vanquished the darkness? Who is this, this new glory, by whose present appearance I am prevented?
4.25: Who is this without sins, who died? Who is this who by [his] light blinded the darkness?
4.26: This is Jesus Christ who was crucified.

5.1: The dead arose; Sheol he trampled; by his death, death he destroyed. After he rose on the third day, he glorified the Father, saying: O God, the Word, undefiled, like as thou who in the Spirit didst call Adam, and madest him live. As saith Moses, and likewise the prophets — we also, in him have we trusted; unto him we give glory; unto whom be glory and power, for ever and ever. Amen.
